key_insight: Machine learning can diagnose degradation mechanisms in simulated lead-free solar cells, but reliable predictions depend on representative training data.
engineering_relevance: For RbSn₀.₅Ge₀.₅I₃ cells, replacing Spiro-OMeTAD with CuI raised simulated efficiency from 19.6% to 21.6%, mainly through improved fill factor.
method: Compared surrogate models trained on factorial grids and Latin hypercube samples.
Identified six degradation mechanisms using multi-label classification of temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit voltage.
evidence_signal: The diagnostic classifier achieved macro F₁ = 0.938 versus 0.687 for physics rules; grid-trained XGBoost fell from R² = 0.9997 on held-out grid points to 0.58 on independently sampled devices, while Latin hypercube training achieved 0.995.
watch_item: The classifier failed to generalize to degradation-mechanism combinations absent from training, and experimental validation remains necessary.
paper_title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements
